title: 7.3.20.1 Idler Pulley Assembly Replacement - Removal (LOTO, side panel access, carriage positioning)
summary: Perform LOTO on the OptiSweep tipper, remove the station side panel if needed to access the motor, then manually position the A-axis and counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base and secure them with M6 socket-head screws to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
when_to_use: Use this procedure to prepare the OptiSweep tipper for the idler pulley assembly replacement removal steps by completing LOTO, gaining motor access via the station side panel (if necessary), and securing the A-axis/counterbalance so it cannot drop when belt tension is released.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Executes LOTO, performs side panel removal (if necessary), positions the A-axis/counterbalance, and threads the M6 socket-head screws to prevent dropping.
safety_notes: Do not proceed without completing LOTO (escalation note).
The procedure includes securing the A-axis and counterbalance to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
access_or_tools_needed: Access to the station side panel securing screws and motor area
Replacement part: Idler pulley assembly (for later steps in the full replacement procedure)

system_preconditions: Tipper is ready for Operator Station Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) per the referenced procedure on page 2.
external_references: Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure referenced on page 2 (name as given in this manual section).

visual_references.description: Figure 7-21: Idler Pulley Assembly diagram showing A-axis/counterbalance carriage positions relative to the threaded holes and the M6 socket-head screws used to prevent dropping.

steps.title: LOTO the tipper
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is locked out/tagged out before any side panel removal or manual positioning work.
steps.instruction: Complete LOTO on the tipper using the procedure referenced as "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is completed for the tipper before proceeding to side panel removal or manual positioning.
steps.failure_condition: LOTO is not completed and work proceeds anyway.

actions.label: Complete Operator Station Lockout/Tagout
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not proceed without completing LOTO.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.20.1: REMOVAL 1. LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove the station side panel (if necessary) to access the motor
steps.purpose: Provide access to the motor area for the subsequent A-axis/counterbalance positioning and belt-tension-related work.
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed (if needed) to access the motor.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panel is removed and the motor area is accessible.
steps.failure_condition: Side panel is not removed when needed for motor access, or removal is attempted without LOTO.

actions.label: Remove nine self-tapping side panel fasteners
actions.exact_action: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and ensure LOTO is complete before proceeding with any side panel removal.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.20.1: REMOVAL 2. If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Position the A-axis and counterbalance between the threaded holes
steps.purpose: Set the A-axis/counterbalance to the correct safe position so it cannot drop when belt tension is released.
steps.instruction: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail; position the carriages between the holes on the respective rails.
steps.expected_result: A-axis and counterbalance carriages are positioned between the threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriages are positioned between the two threaded holes adjacent to each rail (as described).
steps.failure_condition: Carriages cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described.

actions.label: Manually position carriages between threaded holes
actions.exact_action: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail. The carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described, stop and escalate before releasing belt tension.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.20.1: REMOVAL 3. Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail. The carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails.

steps.title: Thread M6 socket-head screws below both carriages to prevent dropping
steps.purpose: Mechanically secure the A-axis/counterbalance so it cannot drop once belt tension is released.
steps.instruction: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages.
steps.expected_result: M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
steps.healthy_condition: M6 socket-head screws are installed below both carriages (as described).
steps.failure_condition: M6 socket-head screws are not threaded into the holes below both carriages.

actions.label: Install M6 socket-head screws below carriages
actions.exact_action: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages. These screws will prevent the A-Axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the A-axis/counterbalance was not positioned between the threaded holes as described (the screws are intended to prevent dropping).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.20.1: REMOVAL 3. ... Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages. These screws will prevent the A-Axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.

success_criteria: Station side panel is removed (if necessary) to access the motor.
A-axis and counterbalance carriages are positioned between the threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
healthy_conditions: LOTO completed before any physical access/removal.
Carriages are positioned between the two threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
M6 socket-head screws are installed below both carriages.
failure_conditions: Carriages cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described.
M6 socket-head screws not installed below both carriages.
escalation_guidance: If the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described, stop and escalate before releasing belt tension.
